sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Hold — unresolved. Oneindig is a small solar EPC, equipment-supply and power-generation group, not a technology platform. The business expanded quickly, but cash conversion and funding discipline have not kept pace. FY26 revenue was ₹71.071 crore and owners’ profit ₹6.085 crore; operating cash flow was negative ₹10.432 crore and cash capex ₹22.811 crore. March funded debt reached ₹46.316 crore, with ₹17.282 crore classified as current maturities and only ₹0.840 crore unrestricted cash.

BQS is 4.3/10. Raw GQS is 5.9, capped at 5.0 because persistent weak cash realization is economically important. IAS is not scoreable. The assessment is not a declaration of lender default: the FY26 auditor and borrower report none. A September item categorized as “Defaults” by a vendor actually discloses a contested consumer-dispute execution warrant served on the MD. The group also received real IPO cash after March, which must not be ignored, but most proceeds are earmarked for working capital and cannot simply retire unsecured loans.

The decisive next evidence is a reconciled post-IPO cash/debt maturity bridge and reliable owner-earnings attribution, followed by actual BSE trading data. Until then, neither a high solar order headline nor a seemingly modest P/E supports an actionable entry price.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Confidence
sections.text:
Research cutoff:20 October 2026; retrieval:22 October 2026. Security: Oneindig Technologies Limited, BSE SME544852, ISIN INE0UR501013. Financials use Indian GAAP/AS. FY23–24 are restated standalone; FY25–26 consolidated. The prospectus’s ten months ended 31 January 2026 are not labeled FY26 full-year results. Latest full audited year is 31 March 2026, with later issuer disclosures considered through cutoff.

The scenario reference ₹128 is assumed, not an authenticated 19 October close. Rolling sites provided conflicting dated intraday observations; no retained historical closing row was validated. Illustrative capital is ₹500,000, not the user’s allocation. Horizon is 20 October 2026 to 20 October 2031, with a 15% nominal pre-tax equity-return hurdle and 12%/18% tests. Economic returns are distinguished from personal taxes and transaction costs.

G1 is Conditional; G2, G3 and G4 are Hold. Confidence is medium in historical operating scale, low in current financing and exact owner economics, and low in implementation liquidity. These holds override an investment classification and exclude the issuer from currently eligible rankings. Historical analytical scores remain visible to explain the business, not to evade the gates.

sections.title: Scorecard Audit
sections.text:
The thirteen primitive factors are GOV4, MOAT3, REV8, DUR5, CAP5, CASH2, BAL3, EXEC5, EARN5, and R/D/P/L not scored. BQS uses 20% GOV,20% MOAT,12% REV,10% DUR,12% CAP,10% CASH,8% BAL and 8% EXEC. It equals 4.30 exactly. GQS weights REV40%, DUR20%, EARN15%, CAP15% and CASH10%, producing 5.90 before the mandatory poor-cash-realization ceiling of 5.00.

IAS reuses unrounded final BQS once at 25%; it does not re-add GQS. Its known quality contribution is 1.075, with 75% missing across R35%, D20%, P10% and L10%. The diagnostic missing-data range is 1.825–8.575, not a confidence interval or score. IAS remains NS without midpoint imputation or renormalization. One-decimal display uses Decimal HALF_UP; classifications use unrounded arithmetic.

Each factor includes source/evidence links, confidence and what would raise or lower it. Medium-confidence revenue evidence cannot justify 9–10 despite fast growth. Weak CASH explicitly constrains GQS; a later verified financing resolution would change the gates, not automatically repair operating cash quality.

sections.title: Business and Economic Engine
sections.text:
Customers buy turnkey solar projects, modules/inverters and related equipment, installation/O&M, or electricity under PPAs. FY26 revenue comprises goods ₹69.0719 crore, services ₹0.1371 crore and electricity ₹1.8620 crore. Thus the “goods” line includes EPC material pass-through; it is not pure software-like recurring revenue. Materials must often be procured ahead of delivery, project acceptance precedes collection and government guarantees tie up deposits.

The group owns 51% of Ziya Solar Energies Three, Ziya Solar Energies Four and Oneindig Jodhpur Solar. The first two operate solar assets, while the third has negligible current revenue. An associate, Green Wattage Oneindig Energy, is reported at 37% ownership; its small carrying value does not eliminate the need to reconcile accounting treatment. Existing SPV capital additions mean the group is increasingly asset-intensive, unlike a pure procurement integrator.

The correct model separates working-capital-intensive EPC cash generation from capital-intensive IPP construction and electricity receipts. Audited EBITDA by these economic segments is not available. The consolidated model therefore discloses scenario IPP earnings/debt allocations, deducts minority economics and tests those allocations; it does not claim a precise sum-of-parts valuation. The office purchased in September is an operating asset already supporting the earnings model, not free additional property value.

sections.title: Moat and Competitive Position
sections.text:
Execution knowledge, supplier relationships and tender qualification may win work, but the evidence does not establish durable pricing power, patents, proprietary technology, a network effect or customer switching costs. EPC and procurement contracts remain competitive and project-specific. The company’s own prospectus identifies established competitors, equipment-price changes, policy dependence and land/permit delays.

Concentration is a direct constraint on bargaining power. FY25’s largest customer contributed 62.19% of revenue and the top three 93.08%; the top ten supplied 96.76%. The top ten suppliers accounted for 99.49% of purchases. January 2026 concentration appears more dispersed at the single-customer level, but the reported top-ten share remains 97.25% and some denominators/labels conflict. Those tables cannot prove diversified recurring demand.

Solarium is a useful solar EPC/distribution comparator, but its larger scale and different residential/government mix prevent a direct premium transfer. Its FY25 revenue ₹230.08 crore and EBITDA₹25.90 crore are historical operating context, not a contemporaneous valuation comp. Waaree-scale incumbents would require separate current financial and price work before quantitative comparison. MOAT3 reflects real execution utility with limited evidence of protected economics.

sections.title: Revenue Growth and Organic Bridge
sections.text:
Revenue rose from ₹19.3199 crore inFY23 to ₹43.6412 crore inFY24, ₹46.0142 crore inFY25 and ₹71.0710 crore inFY26. The last annual increase is 54.5%, after only 5.4% inFY25. The three-year group CAGR is approximately 54.4%, but a smooth CAGR hides project timing and FY24’s unusually large jump.

FY26 electricity revenue of ₹1.8620 crore is separately identified. Excluding it, parent EPC/equipment/services revenue is ₹69.2090 crore, about 50.4% aboveFY25 and a three-year legacy CAGR near 53.0%. This is a better legacy-organic proxy than calling the entire group comparable. Newly formed/controlled SPVs had noFY25 operating revenue; their later build-out is a business-model extension, not evidence of inorganic revenue acquired at a known purchase price. No material seller-acquisition revenue is inserted without evidence.

Growth comes with material cash costs. Receivables rose from ₹11.1263 crore to ₹29.8960 crore, much faster than sales, while inventory reached ₹18.6390 crore. Closing receivable days rose from 88 to 154 using annual sales. These are closing-balance indicators, not average DSO or proof of non-collection. Volume, realized project prices, recurring O&M retention and contract-level cash collection are unavailable, limiting how confidently growth can be extrapolated.

sections.title: Growth Quality, Capital Returns and Runway
sections.text:
The legacy FY23–FY25 bridge increases normalized NOPAT by ₹3.9513 crore against an ₹11.5315 crore increase in an equity-plus-debt-minus-free-cash capital proxy, implying 34.3%. That provides positive evidence for historical reinvestment quality without substituting current ROCE for incremental returns. Restricted operating deposits remain capital employed. The proxy includes some non-operating balances and omits tiny NCI, so it is not a precise project ROIC.

FY25–FY26 is different: incremental NOPAT₹3.7483 crore against capital addition ₹45.0562 crore implies 8.3%, below an explicitly assumed 12–15% capital-cost range. Assets are newly ramping, so this is not a settled lifetime project return. AcrossFY23–FY26 the ratio is 13.6%, but aggregation conceals the shift from EPC to owned power assets. CAP5 recognizes both legacy strength and unproven new capital productivity.

The January order table reports ₹157.5752 crore outstanding across EPC, solar pumps and PPA-related work; it is dated and cannot be treated as October executable backlog. September’s ₹140 crore NHPC announcement is L1 status in a RESCO tariff tender, explicitly not a final award. The 4.8 MW MoU has only ₹0.624 crore rights consideration specified; construction, funding and definitive documents remain distinct. GQS is capped at 5.0 because accounting growth has not converted into cash. Runway is useful only if awarded, executable and financeable.

sections.title: Management, Governance and Execution
sections.text:
Promoters retained 37.80% after an all-fresh IPO, with no offer-for-sale cash-out. That aligns some capital interests, but does not prove governance quality. Related-party procurement from V R Srikaraya was ₹2.1728 crore inFY26 versus ₹6.8563 crore inFY25. MAT Commercial Linkages borrowing/repayment was ₹1.1864/₹0.6886 crore, with ₹0.5899 crore payable. A₹0.375 crore director borrowing is disclosed, while the ₹6.8959 crore long-term director category needs a group-to-related-party-note bridge.

The predecessor audit issue must be described fairly. The restated examiner reproduces a 21 August 2025 explanation that the earlier disclaimer wording was a printing/typographical mistake and corrected to unmodified. The prospectus mixes FY labels and report dates. This is counterevidence to an unresolved disclaimer allegation, although independently authenticated original correction documents would strengthen assurance.

The 24 September filing discloses a consumer-dispute execution warrant served on MD Manoj Agrawal, concerning alleged non-compliance with an 8 January 2025 order. Management says it received neither proper notice nor the order and had no underlying payment/invoice with the complainant; applications sought recall and setting aside. The retrieved record does not establish final adjudication or resolution. It is not a lender default and is not treated as proven fraud. The separate audit-trail and reporting failures remain relevant regardless of that dispute’s merits.

sections.title: Forensic Accounting and Cash Reconciliation
sections.text:
Both main audit opinions and IFC opinions are unmodified, but Rule 11(g) says the parent audit trail was not enabled/operated throughout transactions. That prevents a clean-control inference from the main opinion. CARO reports no lender default or material statutory arrears; its bank-return comparison is not applicable under the stated working-capital sanction threshold. Three subsidiaries were audited by other auditors, whose reports the group auditor relies upon.

The full restated FY25 cash flow is−₹0.4537 crore, versus+₹0.2842 crore in the annual comparative. The ₹0.7379 crore change nearly equals the ₹0.7380 crore shift from gross to net equity proceeds; tax/other-asset classifications also offset. It is mostly classification, not recovered profit. Summary tables in the prospectus do not fully agree with the full statements; full signed statements control. FY24 PAT fell from ₹4.0517 to ₹2.9505 crore after tax/gratuity restatement. FY26 finance interest and borrowing costs total ₹2.8657 crore, while cash-flow addback/payment is ₹2.4494 crore: ₹0.4163 crore needs an accrual/classification explanation.

March cash-and-bank ₹6.4516 crore contains ₹5.6122 crore pledged deposits. Additional noncurrent security deposits of ₹2.4224 crore are also restricted. Cashflow unrestricted cash ₹0.8396 versus note ₹0.8394 is a small ₹2,000 discrepancy. The reserve note differs from the balance sheet by ₹0.0045 crore, matching a reported minority line, but ownership attribution and AOC subsidiary losses do not reconcile cleanly. Associate treatment also needs clarification. These are not automatically fraud, but together with disabled audit trails justifyG2 Hold for exact owner-return analysis.

The earlier ₹9.3406 crore tax demand was subsequently rectified according to the prospectus, which reports ₹1.3590076 crore paid on 9 July 2026. The printed principal/interest do not add to that payment; obtain the challan rather than add all figures. The model pays the March ₹2.3452 crore tax liability once, including July settlement. Performance guarantees ₹4.9456 crore plus guarantees ₹1.24 crore are contingent exposures, not automatically extra funded debt. Mature receivables and related-party terms should be checked before releasing provisions.

sections.title: Valuation, Funding and Price-Implied Expectations
sections.text:
At the explicitly assumed ₹128, postissue shares imply ₹139.829 crore market capitalization and 22.98× FY26 owners’ profit. ReportedEPS₹7.56 is based on pre-IPO shares; current-share normalized historicalEPS is ₹5.57. A mechanical EV using March debt and only unrestricted cash is ₹185.305 crore, or 15.19× normalizedFY26 EBITDA. It is not a current observed EV: IPO receipts and later uses cannot be mixed with old debt without reconciliation, and restricted deposits are not free surplus.

IPO gross proceeds ₹27.648 crore less total fees ₹3.656 crore produce ₹23.992 crore net equity. The already-paid ₹0.15 crore fee means only ₹3.506 crore further fee cash at receipt. ₹20 crore is working-capital earmark, planned ₹14 crore inFY27 and ₹6 crore thereafter; ₹3.992 crore is GCP. The prospectus explicitly excludes repayment of outstanding unsecured loans. Models maintain separate eligible-use pools and do not let IPO money erase an earlier cash trough. July tax and the internally funded ₹2 crore September office purchase are timed before/after receipt appropriately.

Bear/base/bull operating assumptions are 10%/22%/35% revenue growth,13%/16%/18% EBITDA margins and 7×/10×/13× terminal EBITDA. These are stress assumptions, not peer-derived market multiples. Monthly intervals retain taxes, cash interest, NWC, restricted deposits, maintenance/growth capex and principal. Current maturities are paid at the latest FY27 date in the core case, with earlier timing stress. All three cases breach a zero free-cash floor, including before entry. This exposes missing financing/collections under the assumptions, not an observed default. Consequently all ordinary and non-rescue conditional IRRs and 12/15/18% entry ceilings are null. Algebraic terminal EV is not realizable equity after a funding failure.

No rescue dilution is silently assumed. A separate, explicitly counterfactual rescue branch issues whole shares at a 50% discount to the assumed ₹128 and 5% fees before each interval. Pre-entry hypothetical shares differ from actual shares; these are not current targets or committed funds. Discount/fee sensitivities show the dilution cost. Zero-cash survival and economic-reserve shortfalls are separately tracked; July tax is also stressed as an additional liability if its March provision linkage proves incorrect. Minority value is deducted from modeled SPV net enterprise value, with earnings/debt allocation sensitivity rather than tiny book NCI. Terminal operating cash reserve and ongoing reinvestment remain; no NWC liquidation, unpledging, extra office resale or post-exit funding is credited. A required-growth solver is disabled, with no fabricated bracket or root, until current funding and price are verified. Genuine NWC×multiple, NWC×capex, maturity×optional-project and NCI sensitivities are embedded in full.

sections.title: Bear Case and Strongest Counterargument
sections.text:
The bear case is not that solar demand disappears. It is that rapid project execution converts sales into receivables and guarantees while new owned assets require more capital before generating sufficient equity cash. A customer delay, poor bid pricing, discom collection stretch or loan maturity can force a refinance or fresh issue. Higher growth can worsen the cash deficit even while an EBITDA multiple produces an exciting paper valuation.

The strongest counterargument is substantial: legacy revenues and profits grew, legacy incremental return proxies are healthy, new solar assets are only ramping, the group raised real fresh IPO cash, and auditors did not report actual lender defaults. Collections after March may be materially better than the conservative model. This is why the conclusion is Hold for unresolved evidence, not a proven-distress classification or categorical sell.

The thesis-break variables are actual unrestricted cash after IPO deployment, repayment/refinancing of the ₹17.282 crore current maturities, conversion of ₹29.896 crore receivables into cash, and minority-attributable returns from the solar assets. A resolution based only on a larger order headline is insufficient. Conversely, authenticated cash collections and creditor settlement could remove a funding Hold even before a long financial history exists.

sections.title: 5× and10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A multibagger outcome requires owner earnings and realizable equity value, not a large industry target. At assumed market capitalization ₹139.829 crore,5× implies ₹699.146 crore and 10×₹1,398.292 crore equity value before any further issuance. At 15× terminalP/E this requires approximately ₹46.61 crore and ₹93.22 crore owners’ profit respectively, versusFY26₹6.085 crore. At an 8% attributable net margin that would correspond to roughly ₹583 crore or ₹1,165 crore revenue.

The embedded reverse arithmetic includes 5- and 10-year horizons and 10×/15×/20× terminalP/E. It assumes no further dilution and successful financeability, which the present record does not establish. New equity sold cheaply to bridge cash needs can increase corporate scale while reducing each existing share’s participation. A35% revenue-growth bull case is therefore not a 5× prediction.

The practical path would require several independent achievements: diversify customers, win genuinely awarded projects, improve collections, prove after-minority project yields, recycle capital and preserve per-share economics. The model gives no probability to this combination. The company does not meet a high-quality compounder designation withBQS 4.3 and cappedGQS 5.0.

sections.title: Monitoring Dashboard
sections.text:
Before investment eligibility: obtain a dated post-IPO funds-utilization statement and October cash/debt bridge; distinguish pledged deposits, unspent earmarks and actual free cash. Match every current maturity to paid, refinanced or still-due status, with lender dates/terms and no assumed undrawn facilities. Verify that July tax payment is inside the March tax provision and resolve the printed challan arithmetic.

Before upgrading reporting confidence: obtain the FY26 interest cash/accrual bridge, reserve/NCI/51% subsidiary allocation, associate accounting, and a reconciled related-party borrowing table. Confirm audit trails are enabled and retained, and see the next auditor’s specific Rule 11(g) statement rather than a generic clean opinion. Track the consumer execution case through actual court/issuer outcome and keep allegation and defense together.

Before upgrading growth quality: measure cash collected from the largest customers, old-receivable aging, margin deposits/guarantees, certified project completion, own-plant generation/availability and debt-service coverage. Treat NHPC L1 as pending until formal award and project funding are disclosed; track the 4.8 MW MoU only through definitive agreements, permits, full capex and ownership terms. Before implementation, retain actual BSE close/turnover rows, current market lot, spread/depth, circuits and exit-capacity evidence. Reopen scores on new evidence rather than on price movement alone.

sections.title: Final Classification and Conditional Action
sections.text:
Final classification: Hold — unresolved reporting, current funding and tradability. Business quality is low-to-middling at 4.3; growth quality is constrained at 5.0 despite strong historic revenue expansion. IAS is NS. It is not valid to describe this simply as “cheap,” “expensive,” a proven default or a software growth story.

Research priority is to close cash/debt and owner-earnings reconciliation gaps. It is not yet eligible for an investment consideration ranking or a price-trigger buy/watchlist. All ranking flags are false while critical holds remain, although analytical historical scores are preserved. No portfolio allocation, purchase, sale or publication action follows from this dossier.

If reporting and financing are resolved, rebuild with a retained dated BSE price and measured whole-lot liquidity before assigningR, D, P orL. At assumed ₹128, one 1,200-share lot costs ₹153,600; the ₹500,000 reference fits three lots costing ₹460,800, while four lots cost ₹614,400. Those figures show indivisibility, not assured executable size or suitability. A smaller nominal valuation does not remove debt/refinancing and market-exit risks.

sections.title: Sources, Reconciliations and Remaining Gaps
sections.text:
Primary evidence consists of the final prospectus, completeFY26 annual report with standalone/consolidated audits and annexures, August results and signed September NHPC/MoU/property/warrant filings. Where direct BSE retrieval failed, issuer PDFs were obtained from the issuer’s linked Google Drive or a document mirror; original source links, retrieval links and content hashes are retained. Secondary news headlines only helped locate documents. Their financial summaries were not substituted for audited statements.

The complete historical inputs, interim distinction, derived capital/cash calculations, every dated model interval and all sensitivity rows are embedded in the canonical dossier and reproduced by the included builders. Source-safe archives contain factual financial extracts and source hashes, not original documents, OCR, shareholder lists or personal identifiers. Reconstruction verifies calculations from retained extracts; it does not independently reauthenticate excluded originals.

Unresolved gaps are explicit: authenticated cutoff BSE closing/turnover records; current cash and maturity settlement; exact subsidiary equity attribution and debt location; current committed project capex; audit-trail remediation; accrued-versus-paid interest; consistent tax payment arithmetic; original predecessor audit correction; final consumer-dispute outcome; and fresh executable backlog. None is silently set to zero. These gaps determine the holds and the null returns, and provide a bounded checklist for a future update.

summary:
Hold — unresolved. Oneindig is a small solar EPC, equipment-supply and power-generation group, not a technology platform. The business expanded quickly, but cash conversion and funding discipline have not kept pace. FY26 revenue was ₹71.071 crore and owners’ profit ₹6.085 crore; operating cash flow was negative ₹10.432 crore and cash capex ₹22.811 crore. March funded debt reached ₹46.316 crore, with ₹17.282 crore classified as current maturities and only ₹0.840 crore unrestricted cash.

BQS is 4.3/10. Raw GQS is 5.9, capped at 5.0 because persistent weak cash realization is economically important. IAS is not scoreable. The assessment is not a declaration of lender default: the FY26 auditor and borrower report none. A September item categorized as “Defaults” by a vendor actually discloses a contested consumer-dispute execution warrant served on the MD. The group also received real IPO cash after March, which must not be ignored, but most proceeds are earmarked for working capital and cannot simply retire unsecured loans.

The decisive next evidence is a reconciled post-IPO cash/debt maturity bridge and reliable owner-earnings attribution, followed by actual BSE trading data. Until then, neither a high solar order headline nor a seemingly modest P/E supports an actionable entry price.
